patient_summary:
Hello there, you're a 70-year-old gentleman. You were recently admitted to the hospital for managing a fever. You have some health problems like high blood pressure, diabetes, and high cholesterol. You also have a history of prostate issues and had a prostate biopsy. You're currently on antibiotics for a urinary tract infection. 

From your heart, you don't have any significant symptoms except for feeling tired and fatigued. You had a heart operation before, and you have a family history of heart problems. 

Here are the medicines you're taking:
1. Metformin - to help control your diabetes.
2. Metoprolol - to help manage your heart condition.
3. Crestor - to help control your cholesterol.
4. Claritin - to help with your allergies.
5. Flomax - to help with your prostate issues.
6. Prilosec - to help with your heartburn.
7. Folic acid - to help with your health.
8. Metoprolol - to help manage your heart condition.
9. Claritin - to help with your allergies.

If you have any of these symptoms, you should get help right away:
- Fever or chills
- Chest pain or shortness of breath
- Nausea or vomiting
- Urgency in urination

If you have any questions or concerns, please talk to your healthcare team. They are there to help you.
caregiver_checklist: Check Metoprolol dose and schedule twice daily.
Watch for fatigue and tiredness, report to healthcare provider.
Call if fever or chills persist for more than 24 hours.
Watch for shortness of breath, report to healthcare provider.
Call if nausea or vomiting persists for more than 24 hours.
Monitor blood pressure, report to healthcare provider if elevated.
Watch for anxiety, report to healthcare provider if severe.
Call if urinary urgency persists for more than 2 weeks.
Check Metformin dose and schedule as prescribed.

The patient has history of elevated PSA and BPH.  He had a prior prostate biopsy and he recently had some procedure done, subsequently developed urinary tract infection, and presently on antibiotic.  From cardiac standpoint, the patient denies any significant symptom except for fatigue and tiredness.  No symptoms of chest pain or shortness of breath.,His history from cardiac standpoint as mentioned below.,CORONARY RISK FACTORS: , History of hypertension, history of diabetes mellitus, nonsmoker.  Cholesterol elevated.  History of established coronary artery disease in the family and family history positive.,FAMILY HISTORY: , Positive for coronary artery disease.,SURGICAL HISTORY: , Coronary artery bypass surgery and a prior angioplasty and prostate biopsies.,MEDICATIONS:,1. Claritin.,ALLERGIES:,  DEMEROL, SULFA.,PERSONAL HISTORY: , He is married, nonsmoker, does not consume alcohol, and no history of recreational drug use.,PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:,  Significant for multiple knee surgeries, back surgery, and coronary artery bypass surgery with angioplasty, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, elevated PSA level, BPH with questionable cancer.  Symptoms of shortness of breath, fatigue, and tiredness.,REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:,CONSTITUTIONAL:  No history of fever, rigors, or chills except for recent fever and rigors.,HEENT:  No history of cataract or glaucoma.,CARDIOVASCULAR:  As above.,RESPIRATORY:  Shortness of breath. No significant carotid bruits.,LUNGS:  Air entry bilaterally fair.,HEART:  PMI displaced.  S1 and S2 regular.,ABDOMEN:  Soft, nontender.  Bowel sounds present.,EXTREMITIES:  No edema.
